text: Chiara has her driving test on Thursday at 11am. Third attempt, and she's properly nervous about the roundabouts. Text her good luck Wednesday night.
Pick up the dry cleaning before 5 tomorrow and drop the parcel at the post office. Car insurance renewal is due end of the month.
Nikhil is obsessed with chess at the moment. Plays online most evenings and is rated about 1600 now. He wants to enter a weekend tournament in Leeds sometime in early March.
Carmen got her A level results back. Two As and a B, so she's into Sheffield for medicine after all. Must send her a card.
Bridget's grade 6 piano exam got cancelled because the examiner was ill. They're rebooking it for sometime next month, probably a Saturday morning.
Lunch with Gintaras. He's been knitting since lockdown and now sells socks at the craft market on the first Sunday of every month. Very proud of a cable-knit jumper he finished last week.
Yaw sat his ACCA paper on Monday afternoon. Results don't come out until mid-December. I should ask him how he felt it went when I see him at five-a-side.
Book the boiler service for sometime next week, ideally a morning. Also renew my passport before the summer.
Angela and her husband are both doing the Great North Run next September. She's already training three times a week and he has a new pair of trainers he won't shut up about.
Carlos supports Benfica and gets up at stupid o'clock to watch them. Apparently the derby is on the 2nd at 8pm our time.
Blessing failed her theory test by two marks yesterday. She was gutted. Rebooked for the 14th at half 9. Don't forget to message her the hazard perception app I used.
Aidan, or Ado as everyone calls him, is auditioning for the youth orchestra on Saturday at 2pm. Plays cello. His mum says he's barely sleeping.
Julia mentioned she'd love a new set of watercolour brushes, the Escoda ones. Her birthday is early February.
Tiago passed his driving test this morning! First time, only two minors. Congratulate him properly when I see him tomorrow evening.
Need to return the library books by Friday and sort out the council tax direct debit sometime this week.

Chantal's sister Teresa has her bar exam results at the end of the month. Chantal says the whole family is on edge. Teresa has been working at a firm in Manchester for a year already, and her job depends on passing. If it goes well they're planning a dinner at Teresa's favourite Lebanese place sometime early next month.

Hiroshi builds Gundam models, really intricate ones with airbrushing. He showed me photos of one that took him four months. Wants to enter a competition in Birmingham over the summer. His wife Chiara jokes that the spare room is now a paint shop, and he's saving for a proper extraction fan. He asked if I'd come and see his stand if he gets a place.
Call with Ciara. Her son Luca has his eleven plus on the 21st, first thing in the morning. She's more nervous than he is. Remind me to text her that afternoon to ask how it went.
Kate's dog Biscuit had his operation on Tuesday and is recovering well. She's taking the rest of the week off to look after him.
Gym at 7am tomorrow, then food shop. Haircut Saturday at 10.
Wiremu is into fly fishing and ties his own flies. He goes up to the Tweed every October with his brother Andre. They're off again the weekend after next.

Jaya has a viva for her PhD on the 30th at 2pm. She seemed calm on the surface but admitted she's been struggling to sleep. Must check in with her the week before. Her supervisor is away until the 20th, so she's been preparing mostly on her own, and her partner Andre is working nights. She said a mock viva with a friend might help.
Ebony's audition for drama school went really well, she thinks. They'll let her know sometime in the next fortnight. Ask her if she's heard anything next time we talk.
Abigail and Heather have their wedding planned for late August. Abigail's brother is doing the music. Heather wants a cake from that place in Hebden Bridge.

Tamar collects vinyl, mostly seventies soul and jazz. She was hunting for an original pressing of Curtis Mayfield's Superfly. Could be a good Christmas present if I ever see one. She goes record shopping in Manchester most Saturday mornings and knows every shop owner on Oldham Street. Also has strong opinions about cleaning records, which I did not ask about.

Asha has her GCSE mocks starting the week after half term. Her dad says she's revising every night and quite stressed about maths. She's hoping to do further maths at sixth form, so these matter to her. He's found her a tutor for Thursday evenings starting next week. I should drop off my old revision guides sometime before then.
Gustavo said his team's semi-final was called off because of the waterlogged pitch. It's been moved to Sunday the 9th at 11.
Colm has been learning the bodhrán for about a year. He plays at a session in the Crown on Wednesday nights. He'd like me to come along sometime before Christmas.
Varun is doing his CFA level two in early June. Studying around a full-time job at Deloitte, which sounds brutal. I should take him for a coffee sometime next week to break it up.
Siddharth's grandmother died last weekend. The funeral is on Friday at 1pm in Leicester. Send him a message tonight.
Pay the window cleaner, order more printer ink, and cancel the gym trial before the 28th.
Bridget and Colm are going to Lisbon for a long weekend in early November. Their first trip without the kids.

Long chat with Carmen on the phone this evening. Her younger brother Gustavo has his Spanish oral on Tuesday at 10am and is panicking, so she's been practising with him every night. Her own exams are in January, and she's thinking about switching from medicine to biomedical science, though she hasn't decided. She also mentioned she's started climbing at the bouldering wall near her flat twice a week. Remind me to send Gustavo a quick good luck text Monday evening.
Nikhil's mum has her hip operation booked for the 17th. He's driving down the night before and staying the week.

Carlos said his cat Pimenta went missing on Sunday night but turned up yesterday morning, a bit thin. Huge relief. He'd been putting posters up all Monday and knocking on doors. He thinks she was shut in someone's garage. Getting her microchip details updated this week just in case.
Kate Fischer from the book club recommended The Covenant of Water. She's reading three books a month and keeps a spreadsheet of them all. Next meeting is the last Thursday of the month at 7.30.
Hiroshi's daughter passed her grade 3 ballet exam with distinction. He was beaming all through lunch.
Ciara is going through a rough patch at work. Her manager keeps moving deadlines and she's thinking about leaving by the end of the year. Check in with her on Friday.
Must get the car MOT done before the 3rd. Garage opens at 8, so maybe Wednesday morning before work.
Luca plays Football Manager obsessively. He's on his twelfth season with Wrexham and has taken them to the Champions League. Says the new version comes out early November.
Teresa has her citizenship test on Monday morning. She's done every practice paper twice. Wish her luck Sunday evening.
Tiago's partner Ebony is expecting their first baby in late April. Tiago is already reading every book going.
Yaw's band is playing at the Brudenell on Saturday the 15th, doors at 8. He plays bass. I'm going with Asha and Varun.
Angela retires at the end of the month after thirty years at the hospital. There's a leaving do on the 29th from 6pm. Need to chip in for the collection and sign the card before then.
Blessing is taking up pottery. She started a wheel-throwing course on Tuesday evenings and wants her own wheel eventually. Hinted that clay tools would make a good birthday present.
Jaya's brother Siddharth just got his place at Edinburgh for computer science. Starts in September.
Ring the dentist first thing tomorrow morning to move my appointment. Then pick up the prescription.
Wiremu's daughter has her grade 8 trumpet exam on the 12th at half 3. She's been practising the scales in the shed so the neighbours don't complain.
Chantal is training for her black belt grading in taekwondo. It's sometime in early December. She trains four nights a week and has a sore knee from sparring.
Gintaras's driving test was cancelled at the last minute because of the snow. He's annoyed, as the next slot isn't until mid-January. I should send him the link to the cancellation checker app.
Abigail is a massive Doctor Who fan. Has every series on DVD and went to the convention in Cardiff in the spring. Apparently she's dressing up as the Fourth Doctor for Halloween.
Quick note: the plumber is coming Thursday between 8 and 12. I'm working from home that morning.
Andre's knee surgery went well yesterday afternoon. He's home now, on crutches for six weeks. Pop round with some food at the weekend.
Julia Schmidt from work has her German B2 exam on the 6th, then a speaking test a week later. She grew up bilingual but says the grammar section terrifies her.
Heather's mum is turning seventy next Saturday. Big lunch at the Italian place on Sunday at 1. Heather's organising and asked if I know a good florist.
Aidan said Ado's audition went brilliantly and he got into the youth orchestra. First rehearsal is next Wednesday at 6.
Tamar and her partner are moving to Bristol at the end of the month. She's starting a new job at the BBC there in early January.
Things to do this weekend: clear out the garage, take the old sofa to the tip, and finally finish that jigsaw. Maybe a long walk Sunday morning if it's dry.

Spent ages with Colm talking about Gaelic football. He's a Mayo man through and through, still bitter about the final. His nephew made the county minor squad last month, which he's thrilled about. Colm's also coaching the under-twelves on Saturday mornings now and says half of them have never kicked a ball before. Next season starts sometime in February. He asked if I'd help out with the first training session.
Varun had his results day for the CFA level one this morning at 9am. He passed! Already talking about level two in June. Send congrats tonight and maybe a bottle of something at the weekend.
